title: Ukraine's temporary Black Sea corridor ships about 700,000 tonnes of grain by late October 2023
body:
After Russia declined to renew the Black Sea Grain Initiative on 17 July 2023, Ukraine opened its own temporary corridor for commercial shipping in August 2023. On 24 October 2023, Ukraine's Minister of Agrarian Policy, Mykola Solskyi, said about 700,000 tonnes of grain had moved through the corridor. Thirty-eight ships had entered Ukrainian ports and more than 30 had departed, according to the Kyiv Independent.

The Danube ports carried far more. About 2.3 million tonnes of agricultural products went through them in September 2023, and total agricultural exports that month, including road and rail, reached 3.6 million tonnes. Solskyi said that at least 6 million tonnes per month had to be exported for the sector to function properly.

Solskyi said the corridor worked thanks to the support of Ukraine's armed forces and the trust of international partners. Unlike the earlier UN and Turkey-brokered initiative, the new route operated without a Russian guarantee of safe passage and depended on Ukrainian military protection of the shipping lanes along the western Black Sea coast. The shift of traffic toward the Danube ports and the temporary corridor reflected the loss of the earlier arrangement, which had moved nearly 33 million tonnes of food products from three Ukrainian ports between July 2022 and July 2023.
